Executive Complaint Overview

Complaints became more numerous across the complete-calendar-year period through 2022, with account-related products contributing most of the recorded volume. The dataset measures complaint submissions, not proven violations.

Company Response Analysis

A recorded timely response indicator is distinct from satisfactory complaint resolution. Blanks are excluded from the Yes/No timeliness denominator and reported separately.

Recorded response timeliness

Yes divided by Yes + No; excluded records are not treated as No

Public response summary

Complaint Timeline Analysis

The interval is the calendar-day difference between the CFPB's receipt of the complaint and its forwarding to the company. It is not the company's resolution time.

Monthly complaint trend

Month Start, with date-aware sorting

Annual complaint volume & YoY change

YoY shown for complete-year comparisons in 2019–2022 only

CFPB complaint-forwarding intervals

Calendar-day bins; bins are descriptive, not regulatory deadlines

Average forwarding interval by product

Mean calendar days; low-volume categories require caution

Unusually long forwarding intervals

Records above 25 days (greater than the global 99th percentile); 15 longest matching the filters

Interpretation: a complaint is a consumer report, not proof of misconduct. “Date submitted” is the CFPB receipt date; “Date received” is the CFPB-to-company forwarding date. A recorded Yes in the timely field is not a resolution-quality measure. Report coverage ends 28 August 2023. The report is a local, offline interactive companion; the supplied .pbip pointer alone is not a complete reopenable Power BI project.
Source: supplied Consumer_Complaints.xlsx and ConsumerComplaints_DataDictionary.csv; all charts recompute from validated complaint-level data. Open this HTML file locally; no internet or external libraries required.
